explanation: Historical token-price accruals and replay's zero new API accruals are separate integer-nanodollar intervals. A price schedule multiplied by real usage is not an invoice cash payment after credits/discounts.
Real business counts require checksum-verified real-provider response envelopes and recomputed canonical request identities; fixture/local-refusal rows do not establish provider acquisition.

Round completeness requires the immutable full plan declared before the first attempt and exactly one real durable completion for every planned task/sample. Failed HTTP retries remain in costs without invalidating an otherwise completed plan; UNKNOWN, unplanned work and missing completions block it.
Token totals contain known usage only. Missing-usage attempts are counted explicitly; zero known tokens is not a claim that unresolved calls used no tokens.

A cash total additionally requires per-attempt api-settlements.json invoice/credit/discount evidence and checksum-linked compute-charges.json metering for training/evaluation/grading/storage/serving. No tariff, free credit or electricity allocation is invented.

Round total attributes the selected round's historical acquisition cash plus its declared measured compute cash. Replay's new provider spend remains zero; historical acquisition is not charged again. Cached acquisitions from another round need an explicit allocation before a new complete cash round is claimed.
Compute smoke wall times are labelled observations, not summed CPU core-hours or machine rental duration. Some workloads ran concurrently.

Cost per point divides a complete attributable round cash total by 100 times verified rate gain. Nonpositive gain is N/A; inconclusive positive gain is descriptive only. Break-even/amortised success costs need a SHIP quality comparison and measured comparable marginal costs.
